# Overview

`Edge_Topology()` performs miRNA gene interaction (MGI) enrichment
analysis using a topology aware permutation test. For each pathway, it
compares an observed topology based score against scores computed on
degree preserving random rewirings of the background MGI and GGI
network, controlled by `iter`. This method also needs a gene to gene
interaction (GGI) network, in addition to the `background_MGI` needed by
the other methods, since its topology score is computed over the
combined MGI and GGI network. `Edge_Topology` can be computationally
expensive on large, real sized pathway or background data. Consider
increasing `ncores` for large analyses.

This vignette uses the same toy BLCA example data as the package's main
Quick Start vignette. See `vignette("miREA")` for a description of that
data and for running all nine methods together through `miREA()`.

# Required inputs

* `pathway`, a three column data frame with columns `pathway`, `miRNA`,
  and `gene`.
* `mir_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `miRNA`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `gene_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `gene`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `mir_mat` and `gene_mat`, raw expression matrices with samples as
  columns.
* `scoreFun`, the transform applied to the miRNA and gene scores, for
  example `"rank"`.
* `background_MGI`, a two column data frame with columns `miRNA` and
  `gene`, or `NULL` to use the bundled default (see `vignette("miREA")`,
  Step 1, for details on `background_MGI`).
* `GGI_source` or `background_GGI`, selecting the gene to gene
  interaction network (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 1, for details on
  `background_GGI` and `GGI_source`).
* `iter`, the number of degree preserving rewirings per pathway. The
  function default is 1000. This vignette uses `iter = 10` to keep build
  time short on the small toy dataset.
* `seed`, an optional integer for reproducible permutation draws.

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_mat)
data(toy_mir_mat)
data(background_MGI)
```

# Run Edge-Topology

```{r prepare-input}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "Edge_Topology",
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI,
    GGI_source = "Reactome",
    gene_mat = toy_gene_mat,
    mir_mat = toy_mir_mat,
    scoreFun = "rank"
)
```

`input_data$data$Edge_Topology` holds the differentially expressed MGIs.
`input_data$pathway$Edge` and `input_data$pathway_GGI` hold the pathway
MGI and GGI sets. `input_data$dict_MGI` holds the MGI dictionary needed
by the permutation test.

```{r run-edge-topology}
background <- unique(paste0(background_MGI$miRNA, ":", background_MGI$gene))
res <- Edge_Topology(
    MGI = input_data$data$Edge_Topology,
    background = background,
    pathway = input_data$pathway$Edge,
    pathway_GGI = input_data$pathway_GGI,
    dict_MGI = input_data$dict_MGI,
    pvalueType = "neg",
    minSize = 2,
    maxSize = 5000,
    iter = 10,
    ncores = 1,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    seed = 42
)
head(res)
```

# Run through miREA()

`Edge_Topology()` can also be run through the `miREA()` wrapper, which is
useful when you want its result alongside other methods' results in a
single `miREAResult` object (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 2, for the
multi-method case). For a single target, `background` can be a plain
character vector instead of a named list.

```{r run-through-miREA}
result <- miREA(
    methods = "Edge_Topology",
    input_data = input_data,
    background = background,
    pvalueType = list(Edge = "neg"),
    minSize = 2,
    maxSize = 5000,
    iter = 10,
    ncores = 1,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    seed = 42
)
head(result$result$Edge_Topology)
```
